title: OpenAI makes its Jev competitor widely available as decision model competition heats up
slides: OpenAI opens its Jev rival to everyone — why now?
The model was quietly tested with select partners for months
Its edge is structured decisions, not raw language fluency
Teams can now route real decision tasks through it
Test one decision task this week and compare outputs
thread_text:
1. The model nobody saw coming

OpenAI just dropped its Jev rival on the public — after quietly testing it with select partners for months. Why the sudden reveal now?

2. It's not about chat

Its real edge is structured decisions, not raw language fluency. That means it's built for routing real business logic, not writing poems.

3. Your team can use it

Teams can now push actual decision tasks through it — think triage, routing, prioritization. Not just drafting emails.

4. The quiet test phase

Select partners spent months testing it behind closed doors. That head start means early adopters already know where it breaks.

5. Test one task now

Pick a single decision task this week and route it through the model. Compare the output to your current process — then decide.

instagram.caption:
OpenAI just made its Jev rival available to everyone, not just select partners.

It spent months testing quietly with a few teams behind closed doors.

The edge isn't chat fluency — it's structured decisions: triage, routing, prioritization. 🧠

If you build or publish workflows, this is the layer that could replace your manual routing rules — not your writing.

Which single decision in your process would you actually trust a model to route this week? 👇
